narr: Multiple rounds of thunderstorms developed and moved across southeast Arizona from mid morning of August 16 through the early evening of August 17. Individual storms produced heavy rain of 1 to 2 inches per hour, but some locations where multiple thunderstorm events occurred received 3 to 4 inches of rain during the period. The result was numerous reports of flash flooding, road closures and swift water rescues, especially in Pima and Cochise counties. Longer term flooding occurred in the Brawley Wash and downstream in Greene Wash. Damage from thunderstorm winds and lightning also occurred in the Tucson Metro.
ev: One to two inches of rain in less than an hour caused flash flooding in south central Pinal County. Considerable damage occurred to Park Links Rd. between Cattle Tank Rd. and the I-10 Frontage Rd. McClellan Wash also flooded Milligan Rd. resulting in its closure.

One inch of rain in 15 to 30 minutes created flash flooding of washes and roadways in a small portion of east Tucson. A vehicle was stranded in flowing water near 5th St. and Wilmot Rd. Flood waters also crossed roadways in Wilshire Heights near Broadway and Craycroft.

More than one inch of rain in less than an hour caused a rapid rise in Alamo Wash where a storm had produced an inch of rain three hours earlier. A motorist was rescued from a vehicle stuck in floodwaters on Chantilly Rd. at the Alamo Wash.

One to two inches of rain in less than an hour caused flash flooding and road damage in, as well as both north and east of Douglas. One person was rescued from their vehicle in floodwaters on Pedregosa Rd. near State Route 80. Leslie Canyon and Glen Rds. and Washington St. were closed due to flooding. Nine metal gates of the international border wall were damaged by Silver Creek flood waters just west of the San Bernardino National Wildlife Refuge.
Two to three inches in one hour caused flash flooding of washes and several road closures in Oracle.
More than 1 inch of rain in less than an hour in the mountains north of State Rte. 266 caused flash flooding down the mountains and mud and rocks to block a portion of that route.

Two to four inches of rain in less than two hours caused flash flooding from east of Sierra Vista to north of Bisbee to Elfrida. Floodwaters deposited several rocks on State Rte. 80 near N. Old Divide Rd. northwest of Bisbee and caused the closure of Moson and Escapule Rds and the junction of State Rtes. 80 and 90 east of Sierra Vista. Along Davis Rd. near mile post 13, six motorists were rescued from three vehicles amidst floodwaters. Courtland and Jefferson Rds, northwest of Elfrida were also closed due to flooding.
One to two inches of rain in less than an hour caused flash flooding in Picture Rocks. Manville Rd. was closed due to flooding at the Brawley Wash and Sandario Rd. was also closed.

Two to three inches of rain in 2 hours along and south of Highway 86 caused flash flooding south of Ryan Field Airport and around Tucson Mountain Park Estates. Sierrita Mt. Rd. was closed near Hilltop Rd. and both Sandario Rd. and Snyder Hill Rd. was closed at the Black Wash.

One to two inches of rain in two hours caused flash flooding in Marana and Avra Valley. Anway Rd. was closed south of El Camino de Tres Arroyos as well as Silverbell Rd. near the Cocio Wash. Avra Valley Rd. was closed at the Brawley Wash.
